patch.value: Absorb pm-cli 2026.8.3: realign in-process dispatch with the CLI envelope

Both failing tests pass against 2026.8.3 with the genuine defect fixed rather than the assertion weakened; the per-workspace serialization guarantee is preserved; the isSafeTypeFolder traversal guard remains intact; package.json, package-lock.json and node_modules all agree on 2026.8.3.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Diagnosis: (1) Envelope shape — PmClient.run('create'/'update'/'close',...) now returns the flat CLI JSON envelope {id,status,changed_field_count} (byte-identical to the spawned 'pm create --json' output), not the old typed CreateResult/UpdateResult {item,...}. pm-web's runPmInProcess is a pass-through, so the in-process path already agrees with the subprocess path (both flat). The stale consumers are: test/pm-runner.test.ts (reads parsed.item.id / parsed.item.description) and src/routes/{pm,github}.ts import routes (read parsed.item?.id for create, falling back to item[i]/#num and losing the real id). (2) Concurrency — runPmInProcess is dispatched OUTSIDE runSerialized, so in-process actions (create/update/get/...) never acquire the per-workspace tail mutex; same-workspace calls overlap and cross-workspace calls are unbounded. The spawn fallback path is the only one that serializes. Fix: wrap the whole dispatch (in-process attempt + spawn fallback) in a single runSerialized(dir,...) so both paths honor per-workspace serialization with cross-workspace overlap.

value.author: pi-agent
value.text: Fix applied: (1) src/services/pm-runner.ts runPm now wraps the entire dispatch (in-process SDK attempt + spawn fallback) in runSerialized(dir,...) so per-workspace serialization holds for BOTH paths; same-workspace calls serialize, independent workspaces overlap (bounded by the command-slot semaphore). Updated the getPmClient doc comment that wrongly claimed the SDK serializes per-workspace. (2) Corrected stale -wrapper consumers to read the flat CLI envelope: test/pm-runner.test.ts (create -> parsed.id; the update description is now verified via a follow-up , which keeps the {item} shape read commands use); src/routes/pm.ts import route and src/routes/github.ts github-import route now read parsed.id instead of parsed.item?.id (the old fallback silently dropped real item ids). isSafeTypeFolder untouched. Gates: typecheck, build, 259/259 tests, coverage thresholds met, audit, pack dry-run, changelog:check all green. package.json/lock/node_modules all on 2026.8.3.

value.author: claude-code
value.text:
Review round 1 (CodeRabbit) — three findings, two accepted and one refused with evidence.

ACCEPTED (nitpick, but the most valuable of the three): the concurrency test exercised only the spawn fallback. The existing test drives a fake pm via PM_CLI_BIN and uses 'calendar', a spawn-fallback action, so it never reached the SDK dispatch this PR actually changed — the serialization fix was untested.

Writing that test exposed a trap worth recording. The obvious formulation — fire N concurrent same-workspace creates and assert none are lost — PASSES EVEN WITH THE FIX REVERTED, because the SDK keeps its own process-wide queue that already prevents lost writes. Durability cannot discriminate here; only mutual exclusion can. That test would have been a pure coverage illusion, so it was discarded rather than shipped.

The formulation that does discriminate: both paths share one queue per workspace (workspaceTails), so a slow SPAWN action submitted first holds the workspace and an in-process action submitted second must not complete until the spawn finishes. Verified both directions — passes with the fix, and with the fix reverted it fails with 'observed in-process:busy -> in-process:idle -> spawn:busy', proving the in-process path was bypassing the queue. The same test also asserts an independent workspace is not blocked, so it covers the cross-workspace parallelism half of the guarantee too.

REFUSED (Minor, 'compares the read-back description with itself'): false positive. The update passes --description '--not-a-flag' and the assertion compares the read-back description against that same literal, which is the value under test, not a self-comparison. The pre-PR code read the description off the UPDATE envelope (which has no item wrapper, so it was undefined) — that was the real defect and it is what this PR fixed by reading the item back via pm get. No change made; explained on the thread.

REFUSED (Minor, 'node_modules does not match the lockfile'): not reproducible here. package.json, package-lock.json and the installed node_modules all report 2026.8.3; the 2026.7.28 the bot saw was a stale install in its own sandbox, not committed state.

Gates after the added test: typecheck clean, 260/260 tests pass, release:check green.

patch.value: In-process dispatch agrees with the flat CLI envelope and participates in the per-workspace queue, with a test that provably discriminates rather than a coverage illusion.
The in-process and subprocess paths return the same shape, same-workspace calls serialize while independent workspaces overlap, and the folder traversal guard remains intact.
Achieved and merged. 260/260 tests pass, release:check green. CodeRabbit endorsed the test strategy and withdrew both of its other findings as false positives after evidence was provided.

Merged in unbraind/pm-web#80. Two defects fixed. First, stale item-wrapper consumers: pm create --json emits a flat receipt, so src/routes/pm.ts and src/routes/github.ts were silently dropping real item ids and falling back to positional placeholders — the same wrong assumption that broke pm-github and pm-csv this session. Second, runPmInProcess was dispatched OUTSIDE runSerialized, so in-process actions never acquired the per-workspace mutex and concurrent same-workspace calls overlapped; only the spawn fallback serialized. Both paths now share one runSerialized wrapper. Review correctly noted the serialization fix was untested, and writing that test exposed a trap worth remembering: asserting that N concurrent same-workspace writes all survive PASSES WITH THE FIX REVERTED, because the SDK's own process-wide queue already prevents lost writes. Durability cannot discriminate here; only mutual exclusion can. The shipped test interleaves a slow spawn action with an in-process one and asserts ordering — reverting the fix makes it fail. The isSafeTypeFolder traversal guard is intact.
